claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' followed by the indented sub-entry 'VALUE clause, VI-49'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' then '  VALUE clause, VI-49'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 969 (B-57) at 300 dpi and read page-969.md. The markdown source keeps every index entry on its own line in the PDF's order, with each sub-entry indented two spaces under its main entry (e.g. 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' / '  VALUE clause, VI-49'; 'LINAGE-COUNTER' / '  Qualified', '  Special register IV-9'; 'MERGE statement' / '  Imperative statement', '  Segmentation', '  Transfer of control'). The claim itself concedes the entry text and page references match. So the transcription source loses no content and no hierarchy. The complaint is only about how a Markdown renderer would reflow bare lines and about the transcription being inconsistent with pages 961-962. That is markup and formatting, not a content discrepancy, and it does not change meaning on this informative index page. Under the verification rules, a formatting-only difference is rejected.
